newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: IMF sees Swiss 96 GDP down 0.5 pct, up one pct 97.
newsitem.headline: IMF sees Swiss 96 GDP down 0.5 pct, up one pct 97.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund said it estimated Swiss gross domestic product would contract a real 0.5 percent this year and grow one percent in 1997.

It said factors weighing on the economy this year included slower growth among Switzerland's trading partners and pressure on Swiss exports from the past appreciation of the Swiss franc against major currencies.

"In 1996, real GDP is estimated to contract by 1/2 percent with the annual average unemployment rate rising to 4-1/2 percent and CPI inflation of less than one percent," it said in a report by a five-member delegation which spent the past week reviewing the Swiss economy.
The report said other factors depressing GDP this year were a construction slump, restrained private consumption owing to morose sentiment and a major inventory correction.
"Looking to next year, growth prospects appear more favourable," it said. "Real GDP is projected to increase by one percent in 1997 -- somewhat below potential growth," the report said.
The IMF said inflation should continue at around one percent in 1997.
"One bleak spot, however, remains job creation, which is not expected to be sufficient to keep the unemployment rate from rising further in 1997," the IMF said.
The IMF said factors that would encourage growth in 1997 included an expected pick-up in foreign demand for Swiss exports, notably in Germany and France.
Swiss exports would also be helped by a recent weakening of the Swiss franc against the mark and the appreciation that has already taken place of the dollar, sterling and lira against the mark.
"Lower interest rates are also envisaged to help establish the pre-conditions for growth. Thus, domestic demand is forecast to experience some revival."
